fact: NOSi's catalogue of its e-government solutions says the Civilian ID System, working with SNIAC, collects and processes civil registry data on births, marriages, deaths and stillbirths in a stream linking the civil registries to other government systems, and registers the citizen's life events; the page gives no date, so the date is its published year, and no count of offices.

The Civil Registry Code approved by Lei 75/VIII/2014 makes birth and death registrable facts (art. 1) and provides that civil registry acts and processes are drawn up in electronic form (art. 15), birth and death entries declared at a competent office being made by inscription (art. 40); this is what the law requires, not a report of practice.

fact: The Code requires entries to be drawn up in electronic form at the conservatórias, delegations or hospital civil registry posts (arts. 15, 45), a hospital birth to be registered at the hospital post before discharge (art. 76), and acts to be held in the national civil registry database, which any conservatória consults in place of certificates (arts. 6, 36); an entry is made on paper only when the system is unavailable and is then transcribed (art. 41(1)(g)). A legal requirement, not a report of practice.
system: base de dados do registo civil nacional

fact: The Code places electronic requests, communications and notifications under rules set by order of the minister responsible for justice (art. 15) and the electronic archiving of registry documents under terms set by the Director-General of Registries, Notary and Identification (art. 24).
system: base de dados do registo civil nacional

fact: Decreto-Lei 43/2007 allows registry acts to be made in electronic form with an advanced electronic signature (art. 3), has the conservatórias' books kept electronically (art. 4) and lets any conservatória reach the registry databases regardless of territorial competence (art. 11); acts made on paper when the system is down are carried into it afterwards (art. 25), and paper rules still apply until the computerisation of the registry services is complete (art. 24). A legal provision covering civil, commercial, land and vehicle registration, not a report of practice.
system: bases de dados dos registos (registo civil)

fact: The decree-law places the civil registry database, with those of the commercial, land and vehicle registries, in the ownership of the Direcção-Geral dos Registos, Notariado e Identificação, whose Director-General is responsible for their processing (arts. 14 and 16); electronic signature rules are set by the minister responsible for justice (art. 3).
system: bases de dados dos registos (registo civil)

fact: UNICEF's country profile, compiled December 2016 to November 2017, states under both birth and death registration that processing is electronic and that all vital events are recorded directly in the computer using specific applications; marriages are processed the same way.
system: civil registry applications in the conservatórias

fact: UNICEF's profile, compiled to November 2017, states that all vital events are recorded directly in the computer, using applications located in the civil registry conservatórias, with a certificate issued immediately; it does not say where the record is held or that it is held in a national register.
system: civil registry applications in the conservatórias

fact: UNICEF's profile, compiled to November 2017, states that the applications in which vital events are recorded are available in all municipalities of the country, in the civil registry conservatórias, with civil registration services in all 22 municipalities (22 of 22, a share of municipalities); it adds that registration stations exist only in the urban centres of the 22 municipalities, rural communities having been reached by mobile teams during the birth registration project and by registration in health structures then being introduced.
system: civil registry applications in the conservatórias
